entries.title: Ask HN: How do you deal with professional jealousy and getting older?
entries.author: tastyface
entries.current_title: Ask HN: How do you deal with professional jealousy and getting older?
entries.excerpt: I'm a 26 y.o. software dev working on going indie. All my life, I've struggled with procrastination. I find it very hard to sit down and work on a project without an external motivator, and on many nights I end up vegging out in front of the TV or aimlessly clicking around on the internet. As a result, even though I am successful on an absolute scale — CS degree from a top-10, worked at a startup and a large company, enough savings to last a few years of solo development — by
entries.guide_zh: 看到同行成就而焦虑、嫉妒，想独立发展的程序员如何面对年龄增长？

entries.title: Ask HN: Who is hiring? (April 2015)
entries.author: _whoishiring
entries.excerpt: Please lead with the location of the position and include the keywords INTERN, REMOTE, or VISA if the corresponding sort of candidate is welcome. Feel free to post any job that may interest HN readers from executive assistant to machine learning expert to CTO. Please do not post recruiting firms or job boards. PS. No April Fools Day content please.

entries.title: Ask HN: How do you log application events?
entries.author: GaiusCoffee
entries.current_title: Ask HN: How do you log application events?
entries.excerpt: We are currently inserting our logs in an sql database, with timestamp, logType, userId, userAgent and description columns. It makes it trivial for us to debug any event by just querying the db. However, after three and a half years of continued use, the table is now way too large. How do you guys log application events in such a way that extracting information from it is easy, but still keep the size of the logs manageable?
entries.guide_zh: 应用事件目前写进 SQL 表，作者询问更合适的日志记录与查询方式。
